Subject: Re: HIPAA/BAA eligibility  security answers + next steps

Hi Jamie / Alex  thanks for the context and the completed vendor questionnaire (looking through it now). Short answers up front, followed by proposed next steps.

1) SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report covering our hosted and dedicated control environment. The most recent reporting period ended 2026-11-15. We can share the SOC 2 report via our secure portal or under an NDA. Link: https://redwoodinference.secure-portal.com/shared/soc2-summary (I included a one-page summary as attachment).

2) BAA availability: Redwood will execute a BAA. Our standard BAA is attached (Redwood_BAA_Template_v2.pdf). Important deployment notes:
   - Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): Eligible for PHI and is the recommended path for most customers processing PHI because it provides tenant isolation and predictable data handling controls.
   - Private (VPC / on-prem): Fully eligible for PHI; recommended if you need complete network isolation or on-prem processing.
   - Hosted API (multi-tenant public endpoint): Not generally eligible for unrestricted PHI processing. For a limited set of non-persistent, de-identified workflows we may agree to constrained use under strict contractual and configuration controls, but that requires a separate compliance review and is not the default.

3) PHI handling boundaries and recommendations:
   - We recommend Dedicated or Private for any workflow that includes direct identifiers (name, MRN, DOB, contact info) and unstructured clinician notes.
   - For Dedicated/Private: data-in-transit is TLS encrypted, data at rest can be encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM options available), and we can configure retention/auto-delete policies to meet your retention requirements.
   - We do not index or reuse customer data for model training unless explicitly contracted.

4) Questionnaire / Evidence sharing:
   - I will continue processing the Vendor_Security_Questionnaire and can provide evidence (config screenshots, control descriptions).
   - If you require the full SOC 2 report, please confirm whether an NDA is preferred; we will route the report through the secure portal once the NDA is in place.

5) Proposed next steps (I recommend these in order):
   a) MedCare returns the completed Vendor_Security_Questionnaire (if not already done).
   b) MedCare confirms the specific retention and KMS requirements (customer-managed keys needed?).
   c) We run a short technical call (1530m) to walk through Dedicated vs Private network/data flows and confirm any IP allowlisting or VPC peering needs.
   d) Once controls are aligned, Legal can sign the BAA and we can spin up a Dedicated pilot environment for testing.

No immediate red flags based on the initial volume you described. Happy to set up the technical call  Marissa, can you propose a few slots?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
